Somewhere in Maryland, there are children who will one day cure a disease at the National Institutes of Health or build the next great telescope at Goddard.

But we have to put science within their reach.

The Maryland Science Center has done that for over 15 million people –  and I’m proud that Maryland’s helping to replace their aging HVAC system and keep this building running strong.

In this moment of fear for our immigrant communities, we will not stand by while bad actors defraud our neighbors.

Not today. Not tomorrow. Not ever.

When a family on the Shore needs answers, they will get them from a qualified attorney – not from someone preying on fear and profiting off of it.

posts.text:
I had the honor of presenting a citation to Warden LaMonte Cooke — the first African American deputy in Kent County and the longest serving local corrections officer in Maryland.

I was also proud to be the first Governor to attend an MCAA Awards Banquet in 49 years.

MCAA and our state’s correctional professionals provide a valuable service, from championing alternatives to incarceration, supporting people pursuing careers in criminal justice, and developing programs to help those in custody.

Dawn and I are praying for the Baltimore County police officer shot earlier today in Pikesville while responding to a report of suspicious activity.

We condemn violence against any and all law enforcement officers in the strongest possible terms. My team is closely monitoring the situation for updates and hope for the officer’s swift and complete recovery.

posts.text:
When I visited Midland, I became the first sitting Governor to do so in its recorded history. But my visit wasn't about the milestone. It was about the people.

Mayor Monahan and the Midland community deserve support from the state, and our FY 2027 budget does just that by funding the restoration of George's Creek riverbed to prevent future breaches and protect local homes and public parks.

Every community in Maryland deserves to be seen. This is what that looks like.
